thread:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - multigpu training jobs failing on node-7 (NCCL comm errors) :rotating_light:

oncall-janet: picking this up. seeing repeated pages from infra monitor.

ben-sre: quick summary from alerts: GPUs on node-7 flapping, container OOMs then GPU driver XIDs, followed by NCCL communicator timeouts. multiple pipelines hit.

ana-ml: customer-visible errors: 502s from model-inference pool for a few customers using pipeline-parallel configs. some retries succeed but latency spikes.

carter-dev: logs from the most recent job:
```
E NCCL WARN init attempt 3: ncclCommInitRank failed, error UnhandledCudaError (0x7f)
E runtime: cuda driver reported Xid 137 on GPU 2, process 14567 (trainer)
W collective: allreduce timeout after 120s, attempts=4
```

ben-sre: dmesg shows repeated GPU reset messages and GPU 2 showing ECC/PCI errors before reset.

mike-runtime: on node-7 we see container restarts (OOM killed) then the runtime tries to rejoin communicator and flaps. This causes rendezvous leader election thrash -> cascade.

oncall-janet: first mitigation: cordon node-7, drain running jobs gracefully where possible, and shift new pipeline-parallel jobs away. Doing now.

oncall-janet: `kubectl cordon node-7` and start evicting non-interactive jobs.

carter-dev: recommending immediate fallback route: switch pipeline-parallel requests to single-device model variant for the affected customer traffic while we stabilize. Can the routing layer do a per-customer fallback?

louise-support: yes please. Customer A (acct 8392) hit rate ~20 rps on that pool, notifying them of degraded performance and fallback ongoing.

ana-ml: set routing rule to prefer model-variant:v1-single-gpu for customers with in-flight errors. That reduces perf but keeps correctness.

mike-runtime: collecting core dumps and nvidia-smi output. Commands I ran:
```
# capture stats
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-dump.csv &
sudo journalctl -u docker -n 200 > /tmp/docker-journal.log
# dump NCCL debug
cat /var/log/runtime/nccl_debug.log | tail -n 200 > /tmp/nccl-tail.log
```

carter-dev: sharing nccl tail snippet:
```
[NCCL WARN] rank 1 -> rank 2 : TIMEOUT waiting at barrier, last barrier seq 1042
[NCCL INFO] Releasing communicator 0x7f8b9c00
[CUDA ERROR] cuCtxDestroy: unknown error (after reset)
```

ben-sre: I've requested a hardware scan from node provisioning team; scheduling GPU swap if errors persist. For now, keep node cordoned.

oncall-janet: action list I want tracked:
- [janet] cordon/drain node-7 (in progress)
- [mike] collect logs and core dumps, upload to incident storage
- [ben] run hardware diag / escalate to provisioning
- [carter] deploy routing fallback for affected customers
- [ana] customer comms and impact tally

ana-ml: customer comms note: impacted customers: Customer A, Customer D, some internal load tests. Estimated affected requests ~3% of total inference traffic across all regions for the hour window. Will send an initial status to customers now.

louise-support: sending message to Customer A: "We're seeing GPU-level instability affecting some pipeline-parallel workloads. We're failing over to single-GPU variant for your requests to maintain availability. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA."

mike-runtime: uploaded logs: s3://redwood-incidents/4281234567/node-7-logs.tar.gz

carter-dev: I pushed routing change as a hotfix: `route: model/pipeline -> model/single-gpu if nccl_failures>3`; monitor in console.

incident-bot: Deploy OK - routing-change-4281 applied by carter-dev :white_check_mark:

oncall-janet: we're seeing immediate reduction in 502s for Customer A. Good. But there are still OOM kills on node-7 for system services; keep cordoned.

ben-sre: diag results in: PCIe link error counter increasing on GPU 2; provisioning suggests replacing the card or re-seat connector. ETA for physical swap ~3 hours.

ana-ml: what's the long-term plan to avoid cascading NCCL leader thrash? We should fail the job early on repeated NCCL init failures instead of retrying and causing cluster noise.

carter-dev: agree. I'll open a follow-up PR to change runtime: if NCCL init fails > 2 times within 30s, mark task unhealthy and let orchestrator reschedule rather than retry in-place. Quick patch ETA 2h.

mike-runtime: note for postmortem: collect per-request token counts and which variants served, record latency/err rate delta for the fallback window. Also save all NCCL debug levels + kernel logs.

louise-support: customers notified. Customer A acknowledged fallback and asked for ETA; told them hardware swap ETA ~3h and we'll follow up when node replaced.

oncall-janet: handoff: I'll remain until the provisioning update, then pass to ben-sre for long-term remediation and to carter-dev for runtime changes.

ben-sre: after swap, we'll run extended burn test 1h before uncordoning. If burn test passes, will uncordon and slowly ramp pipeline-parallel jobs back.

mike-runtime: collected gcore from PID 14567 and uploaded. Also saved container oom logs.

carter-dev: opened tracking ticket INC-4281234567 in our incident board with action items and owners.

incident-bot: Reminder: Pager rotation to ben-sre in 1h.

oncall-janet: thanks team. I'll update the incident channel and post a brief summary for SOC and support.

louise-support: creating customer follow-up template for post-incident report.

ana-ml: quick note: root cause candidate so far - intermittent GPU/PCIe hardware error causing resets, which triggers NCCL re-init storms during pipeline-parallel rendezvous. Primary mitigations: cordon node, fallback routing, hardware swap, runtime guardrail to avoid retry thrash.

ben-sre: will update when provisioning confirms swap complete. Leaving handoff to me at 4281234599.

oncall-janet: handing off. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
